rejected.headline: Martin County investigators warn of counterfeit Pokémon card scams after collectors lose $1,200

lead_independence.headline: Martin County investigators warn of counterfeit Pokémon card scams after collectors lose $1,200
lead_independence.lead: The Martin County Sheriff's Office is investigating two separate cases involving counterfeit Pokémon cards after victims reported losing a combined $1,200 in deals arranged through Facebook Marketplace. In the first case, a collector met a seller at a gas station in Hobe Sound to trade nine Pokémon cards and cash. Investigators said the seller rushed through the transaction and left before the cards could be inspected. Once home, the victim realized the cards were counterfeit, and the seller blocked him online.

rejected.headline: Martin County neighbors report dogs suffering next door as sheriff says legal barriers prevent investigation

lead_independence.headline: Martin County neighbors report dogs suffering next door as sheriff says legal barriers prevent investigation
lead_independence.lead: Public records obtained by WPTV show Martin County Animal Control officers and sheriff's deputies have visited the home at least 11 times since 2020, all related to concerns about the dogs and their owner. One incident report from 2020 describes accounts of as many as 25 dogs inside the home. On multiple occasions, authorities noted feces on the floor and furniture. Records show the owner did clean up after initial visits and told animal control she had re-homed some of the dogs, but she eventually stopped allowing law enforcement inside.

rejected.headline: Palm Beach County cities push for more trees and shade as extreme heat bakes neighborhoods

lead_independence.headline: Palm Beach County cities push for more trees and shade as extreme heat bakes neighborhoods
lead_independence.lead: Palm Beach County Parks and Recreation says the number one need they hear from people, aside from beach access, is shade. Community Greening, a South Florida nonprofit, says adequate tree canopy coverage is around the 30 to 40 percent range and virtually every city in Palm Beach County is at least in the 20 percent range and most are lower. The nonprofit has helped plant and give away nearly 30,000 trees across Palm Beach, Broward and parts of Martin County over the past decade.

rejected.headline: State lawmaker challenges Fort Pierce Causeway Cove development over zoning compliance

lead_independence.headline: State lawmaker challenges Fort Pierce Causeway Cove development over zoning compliance
lead_independence.lead: State Rep. Dana Trabulsy told Fort Pierce city commissioners Monday that the proposed Causeway Cove development does not meet the zoning requirements of Florida's Live Local Act, the same law she supported in 2023 that allows developers to bypass local height and density restrictions. The Causeway Cove project would transform the existing Causeway Cove Marina into a mixed-use development featuring more than 900 apartments and condos, restaurants, and a hotel tower reaching nearly 200 feet in height.

lead_independence.lead: Fort Pierce police are investigating a hit-and-run crash that injured two children who were crossing a street in a marked crosswalk. The crash happened at North 25th Street and Avenue M, where an early-2000s gold Mercedes-Benz was turning from Avenue M onto North 25th Street when it struck the children. The driver initially stopped and checked on the children before fleeing the scene.

lead_independence.lead: Malachi Jenkins, 12, said he was mad when a driver struck his 8-year-old sister Serenity and then drove off at the intersection of North 25th Street and Avenue M in Fort Pierce over the weekend. People ran up to check on her, and she started crying before briefly losing consciousness and then waking back up.

lead_independence.headline: Vero Beach moves forward on $4.7 million Humiston Beach boardwalk reconstruction four years after Hurricane Nicole
lead_independence.lead: Vero Beach has established a five-person committee to help rebuild the boardwalk at Humiston Beach, which Hurricane Nicole destroyed four years ago. The city currently has $3.1 million raised toward the $4.7 million project cost, leaving a $1.6 million funding gap that the new committee will work to close through donor outreach and fundraising.

rejected.headline: Property tax increases push Treasure Coast resident to relocate to Puerto Rico

lead_independence.headline: Property tax increases push Treasure Coast resident to relocate to Puerto Rico
lead_independence.lead: A Treasure Coast man said rising property taxes in Florida pushed him to leave the state and buy a home in Puerto Rico, where he pays nothing in property taxes. Jock Tate now lives in Salinas, Puerto Rico, in a 3-bedroom home he purchased for $95,000. As a disabled veteran, he qualifies for exemptions that eliminate his property tax bill entirely.
